title: Opaque lot identity, source model, and quantity invariants
summary: Create tenant-scoped opaque lot records, source/receipt attribution, unit-aware balances and immutable movement identity so a visible lot label never acts as stock truth or a reusable identifier.
steps: Define opaque lot IDs, permitted display labels, source/receipt links, lifecycle state and tenant isolation.
Represent every received, counted, reserved, allocated, depleted, released and corrected quantity as a revisioned lot movement.
Enforce unit conversion, non-negative allocatable balance and conservation invariants at the command boundary.

positive: A tenant can trace one allocated line quantity through its exact lot movements and source revision.
negative: A typed lot label, cross-tenant ID, rounding conversion or repeated request cannot create, merge, over-allocate or silently rewrite a lot balance.

doneConditions: LOT-V01–V05 preserve opaque identity, source attribution, unit precision, lifecycle and a truthful no-lot state under tenant and concurrency tests.
requiredEvidence: Lot migration, movement conservation property drive, cross-tenant denial trace and historical replay.

title: Shared LotSplitEditor control and accessible split semantics
summary: Build the shared typed split editor used by receipt, count and allocation flows, including slider, exact quantity field, add-lot row, assigned/unassigned summary, validation and review state.
steps: Use one typed editor contract for lot context, total, entries, unit precision, available choices and command revision.
Keep slider and exact numeric field synchronized without hidden rounding; keyboard input remains a first-class route.
Allow adding a discovered/new lot only through the same validated draft, with review, cancel and focus-return behavior.

positive: Changing the slider or exact field updates the same draft total and exposes assigned versus unassigned quantity.
negative: A slider movement, new-lot row, blur, close or retry cannot save an invalid split, lose a draft or claim a received/allocation result.

doneConditions: LOT-S01–S08 have labelled control, keyboard, validation, dirty-close, conflict, offline and status-copy tests in each calling flow.
requiredEvidence: Shared editor component tests, keyboard drive, precision property tests and dirty-draft recovery trace.

title: Receipt and physical-count split flows
summary: Wire receipt and physical-count flows to the shared lot editor so received totals and counted totals remain distinct evidence, with source, suggested allocation, discovered-lot and review/save results.
steps: Record a receipt against supplier/source evidence, received total and explicit lot split before accepting stock.
Record a physical count as a distinct observed-after total with suggested but reviewable per-lot allocation.
Persist discovered lot provenance, validation result, actor/revision and idempotency receipt for each accepted flow.

positive: A saved receipt or count produces one reviewable movement set whose exact total equals the accepted evidence total.
negative: A predicted amount, slider display, stale count, missing source, duplicate save or unresolved difference cannot become a recorded balance.

doneConditions: LOT-R01–R06 and LOT-C01–C07 expose separate receipt/count state, per-lot validation and post-save results with retry-safe tests.
requiredEvidence: Receipt/count integration drives, split conservation checks, duplicate-submit test and stale-revision recovery trace.

title: Reservation, allocation, reassignment, and depletion per lot
summary: Implement albarán-facing lot eligibility, reservation, allocation, reassignment and depletion commands that preserve line/document snapshots and never promise availability from an unaccepted action.
steps: Resolve eligible lots by exact SKU, unit, lifecycle, reservation policy, tenant and current revision.
Make reserve, allocate, reassign, release and depletion idempotent state-specific commands bound to a document line.
Expose accepted allocation/history separately from pending, unavailable, conflict, depleted and provider-independent fulfilment state.

positive: A permitted allocation links an exact line revision to eligible lot quantities and leaves a replayable outcome history.
negative: Two editors, repeated action, a stale lot balance or a depleted/ineligible lot cannot over-reserve, duplicate-deplete or change an issued line snapshot.

doneConditions: LOT-A01–A08 cover line context, eligibility, reserve/allocate/reassign/deplete, history and exception/recovery behavior under concurrency tests.
requiredEvidence: Concurrent allocation drive, idempotency test, issue-snapshot replay and depletion/reassign recovery trace.

title: Lot detail, traceability, recall and document consequences
summary: Expose a safe lot dossier for source, movements, linked lines, recall scope, edit trace and lifecycle while preserving protected data and document/output consequences.
steps: Project a permission-scoped lot dossier with source, movement, linked-line and recall facts at their actual revisions.
Model recall/hold as explicit lifecycle commands with scope, reason, actor and operational consequences.
Preserve document snapshots and safely redact unavailable source/person data without erasing necessary trace identity.

positive: An authorized recall can enumerate its exact affected lot/line scope and retained document consequences.
negative: A generic stock badge, unrelated SKU, archive/redaction action or unscoped actor cannot disclose or change a lot traceability history.

doneConditions: LOT-D01–D06 have auditable source/movement/linked-line/recall/lifecycle views, permission denials and unavailable-state copy.
requiredEvidence: Recall scope drive, permission/redaction test, issued-document history replay and audit query.

title: Lot migration, recovery, evaluation and release gate
summary: Migrate legacy stock safely into explicit lot/no-lot states, rehearse rollback and projection recovery, and gate release on invariant, accessibility and end-to-end evidence.
steps: Classify legacy balances as source-backed lots, explicit unassigned/no-lot balances or quarantined records; never invent provenance.
Rehearse migration, rollback, projection rebuild and operator recovery with per-tenant evidence.
Run split/editor/receipt/count/allocation/recall accessibility, concurrency, conservation and release-gate suites before owner-go.

positive: A migration replay preserves every known balance and labels unknown lot provenance rather than fabricating a source.
negative: A failed backfill, partial projection or release dashboard can neither hide a conservation failure nor mark lot work production-ready without actual evidence.

doneConditions: LOT-12 release checks prove migration/recovery plus all LOT-V/S/R/C/A/D control anatomy, state and invariant gates.
requiredEvidence: Per-tenant migration rehearsal, rollback/rebuild trace, full invariant suite, accessibility drive and release evidence-board entry.

title: Assign stock to lots and zero-net reassignment
summary: Port the Product Sheet action “Assign stock to lots” as physical attribution of a fixed Recorded balance between named lots and Unassigned stock, with typed new lots, zero-net movement history and no albarán fulfilment effect.
steps: Open only from an exact SKU with an evidence-backed Recorded balance and current inventory revision.
Use the shared LotSplitEditor to move the same recorded quantity among named lot IDs, a typed new lot and explicit Unassigned stock.
Record a zero-net attribution/reassignment event with reason, actor, before/after split and revision; do not reserve, allocate, deplete or alter an albarán line.

positive: Saving a valid split preserves the exact Recorded balance, creates a traceable zero-net history entry and names the resulting lot/unassigned composition.
negative: A slider, typed lot, stale revision, repeated save or reassignment cannot create stock, promise availability, change an albarán allocation or hide an unassigned remainder.

doneConditions: LOT-L01–L07 cover action entry, fixed balance context, split/reassignment, typed new lot, unassigned remainder, review/save result and zero-net history with keyboard/concurrency tests.
requiredEvidence: Physical-attribution integration drive, zero-net invariant/property test, stale-revision recovery trace and product-sheet accessible-name/state copy review.
